references.text: The Levites were not numbered with the other tribes, as the Lord had commanded Moses. This is the original command referred to in Numbers 2:33.
The special role of the Levites regarding the tabernacle explains why they were kept separate from the other Israelites in the census.
The Levites were numbered separately according to the Lord's command to Moses, confirming that they had a distinct status.
The separate counting of the Levites (22,000) shows that they were treated differently from the rest of Israel.
Also in the second census, the Levites were not counted among the children of Israel because they received no inheritance among them.
The tribe of Levi was set apart to carry the ark of the covenant and to serve the Lord, and therefore they received no share of the land.
The Levites had no inheritance in the land because the Lord himself was their inheritance, which explains their special position.
The tribe of Levi received no inheritance because the offerings of the Lord were their inheritance, in keeping with their distinct role.
